acceptance: Codex usage-limit failure can fall back to the isolated Claude backend; other Codex failures refuse
Explicit REVIEWER=claude uses the same review record and publication invariants
Real isolation probe denies credentials, primary clone, /tmp, writes, commands, network and custom MCP access
A real dry-run produces a valid record without publication
Focused tests and required CI pass, PR merged
context: Implemented on feat/remote-review-fallback: c42ca7ddf plus fix commit 71bf492fd. PR #3163 opened and armed 2026-10-19; merge pending CI. Independent contract review found 2 Required defects, both fixed: (1) Codex usage-limit classification now only from structured error events, with regression test for unstructured output mentioning the phrase; (2) Claude login staging drops refreshToken and refuses expired logins — real probes proved accessToken+expiresAt-only staging fails Claude CLI auth (Not logged in) while login-minus-refreshToken authenticates. Focused suite 123 passed; real REVIEWER=claude DRY_RUN=1 on PR #3143 head a0997e75 returned approve in ~54s with no publication. Codex-based security reviewer agent failed twice on Codex usage limit (the motivating failure); parent verified credential/isolation paths directly plus real isolation probe by implementing agent.
description: Owner approved a Claude-subagent fallback for checkout-free review when Codex is unavailable because of its usage limit. Share the existing pinned-input, computed-disposition, publication and record pipeline. Restrict file tools to exported base-rule inputs and head tree, disable commands/network/MCP/user customization, and disclose the fallback family without adding an unapproved arm gate. Preserve other Codex errors as refusals.
